import html from typing import List # Example template – in real usage this would be defined elsewhere. USER_POST_FORMAT = """

{post_heading}

{content}
{labels}
""" def render_blog_post( author_id: str, post_heading: str, content: str, labels: List[str] ) -> str: """ Render a secure HTML representation of a forum post. Parameters ---------- author_id : str Identifier of the post's creator. post_heading : str Heading/title of the user's post. content : str Main content/body of the post. labels : List[str] Tags/labels associated with the post. Returns ------- str XSS‑protected HTML string for the forum post. """ # Escape all user-supplied data to avoid injection safe_author_id = html.escape(author_id, quote=True) safe_heading = html.escape(post_heading, quote=False) # quotes not needed in headings safe_content = html.escape(content, quote=True) # Wrap each label in a and escape it escaped_labels = [ f'{html.escape(label, quote=True)}' for label in labels ] # Join the tags with a space to avoid concatenation issues safe_labels = " ".join(escaped_labels) # Use the template with explicit keyword arguments to avoid accidental injection rendered = USER_POST_FORMAT.format( author_id=safe_author_id, post_heading=safe_heading, content=safe_content, labels=safe_labels ) return rendered
